title: Define the Benefits of the AWS Cloud

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS does not expect you to begin by memorizing a giant list of services. First, understand why an organization would use the AWS Cloud.
bullets: The value proposition of the AWS Cloud
Economies of scale and potential cost savings
Benefits of global infrastructure: speed of deployment and global reach
Advantages of high availability, elasticity, and agility
sections.callout: What business or technical advantage does the AWS Cloud provide in this scenario?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
paragraphs: Use the scenario's primary outcome to identify the cloud benefit.
bullets: Reach customers around the world → Global reach
Grow and shrink resources with demand → Elasticity
sections.callout: DEPLOY → REACH → STAY UP → SCALE → MOVE FAST

sections.title: AWS Cloud Value Proposition
paragraphs: A value proposition explains why something provides value. Organizations can consume computing resources without building and operating all underlying physical infrastructure themselves.
Traditional infrastructure can require sizing, purchasing, delivery, installation, cabling, and configuration before an application launches. AWS resources can be provisioned as needed.
sections.callout: A question asking generally why a business would move workloads to AWS points to the AWS Cloud value proposition.

entries.title: Speed of Deployment
paragraphs: Cloud resources can be provisioned much faster than traditional physical infrastructure can usually be purchased and installed.
entries.memoryHook: Do not wait for the server truck. When the clue asks when infrastructure can be ready, think speed.

entries.title: Global Reach
paragraphs: AWS infrastructure lets organizations deploy workloads closer to users in different geographic areas without building their own facilities around the world.
entries.memoryHook: Go where the users are. When the clue asks where the business can expand, think reach.

sections.title: Economies of Scale
paragraphs: AWS combines demand from many customers and operates infrastructure at enormous scale. That scale can create purchasing and operating efficiencies that an individual organization may not be able to achieve on its own.
bullets: Potential cost efficiencies passed through cloud pricing
sections.callout: MANY CUSTOMERS + MASSIVE SCALE → ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY

sections.title: High Availability
paragraphs: High availability means designing systems so services remain available and accessible despite failures or disruptions. The goal is to reduce service interruption.

sections.title: Elasticity
paragraphs: Elasticity is the ability to adjust resources as demand changes. Capacity can increase during a traffic spike and decrease again when demand falls.
sections.callout: ELASTIC = ACCORDION: demand up → resources expand; demand down → resources contract.

sections.title: Agility
paragraphs: Agility is the ability to move quickly, experiment, adapt, and respond to changing requirements. Teams can provision resources, test an idea, learn, and change direction without lengthy procurement.
bullets: Reduce the time required to try something new

table.caption: Match the scenario clue to the AWS Cloud benefit

entries.title: Speed of Deployment vs. Global Reach
paragraphs: Need infrastructure quickly → Speed of deployment. Need infrastructure in additional geographic locations → Global reach.

entries.title: Speed of Deployment vs. Agility
paragraphs: Deploy infrastructure quickly → Speed of deployment. Experiment, adapt, and respond quickly → Agility.

entries.title: Economies of Scale vs. Elasticity
paragraphs: Provider scale creates economic efficiency → Economies of scale. Workload capacity changes with demand → Elasticity.

entries.title: High Availability vs. Elasticity
paragraphs: Failure or downtime → High availability. Changing demand → Elasticity.
